name: Tianyulong
sum: A small heterodontosaurid from the Middle to Late Jurassic of Liaoning, China, preserved with long filament-like structures on its neck, back and tail.
wsnote: About 70 cm long, of which about 44 cm was tail, estimated from Heterodontosaurus because the known specimens are incomplete.
holotype: STMN 26-3, most of the skull and skeleton, in the Shandong Tianyu Museum of Nature; privately collected, from Jianchang County, western Liaoning, with uncertain stratigraphy.
material: Five further specimens: four undescribed in the Shandong Tianyu Museum and IVPP V17090, a nearly complete but partly unprepared skull with vertebrae and limbs, described by Sereno in 2012; all are of uncertain provenance.
exceptional: Long filamentous integumentary structures along the back, tail and neck, resembling those of some theropods.
biology: The filaments suggest homology with feathers and that early ornithischians may have had dermal filaments. Heterodontosaurids are herbivorous or possibly omnivorous.
author: Zheng et al. 2009

dates_note: The holotype was first assigned to the Early Cretaceous Jehol Group; a date of about 158.5 Ma on overlying volcanic rocks puts it in the Middle to Late Jurassic, in the Tiaojishan (Lanqi) Formation and the Daohugou Biota. PBDB uses the Jurassic age.
